The Sabbath (al-Sabt) is a verbal noun from "sabbata al-Yahud," meaning the Jews observed their Sabbath by magnifying it. The meaning is: the punishment of the Sabbath, which is transformation (al-maskh), was only imposed upon those who differed concerning it, and their difference concerning it was that they made hunting permissible in it at one time and forbade it at another time. What was obligatory upon them was that they should agree on its prohibition with one word, after Allah had made it binding upon them to refrain from hunting in it and to magnify it.

The purpose of mentioning this is similar to the purpose of the parable of the town that disbelieved in the blessings of Allah, and other things mentioned, which is to warn of the wrath of Allah against the disobedient, those who oppose His commands, and those who cast off the yoke of His obedience. If you ask: what is the meaning of judging between them when they were all either permitting or forbidding it? I say: its meaning is that He recompenses them according to the consequence of their action, in that they were at one time permitting and at another time forbidding it.

Another explanation: Musa, peace be upon him, commanded them to make one day in the week a day of worship, and that it should be Friday. They refused him and said: "We want the day on which Allah finished creating the heavens and the earth, which is Saturday." Except for a small group among them who were content with Friday. This was their difference concerning Saturday, for some of them chose it and some of them chose Friday over it. So Allah permitted them Saturday and tested them with the prohibition of hunting in it. Those who were content with Friday obeyed the command of Allah, so they did not hunt on it, but their descendants did not restrain themselves from hunting, so Allah transformed them, and not those others. And He will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection, and each of the two groups will be recompensed according to what it deserves.

The meaning of "made the Sabbath" (ja'ala al-sabt) is: it was made obligatory upon them to magnify it and to refrain from hunting in it. It is also read as "innama ja'ala al-sabt" with the verb in the active voice (al-bina' lil-fa'il). And Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) read: "Inna anzalna al-sabt."

To the way of your Lord, that is, to Islam, with wisdom, meaning with a sound, firm argument, which is the proof that clarifies the truth and removes doubt; and with fair admonition, which is that whereby they cannot fail to see that you are advising them and intend what benefits them in it. It is also permissible that the Qur'an is meant, i.e., call them by the Book, which is wisdom and fair admonition; and argue with them in the best manner, meaning by the method that is the best of the ways of disputation, namely gentleness and softness, without harshness or coarseness. Indeed your Lord knows best who among them is astray. So whoever has good in him, a little admonition and slight advice suffice for him; but whoever has no good in him, stratagems fail with him, and it is as if you were striking cold iron.

The first act is named by the name of the second for the sake of parallelism (al-muzawaja). The meaning: if they deal with you in an evil manner, such as killing or the like, then respond with its like and do not exceed it. It was also recited: "And if you retaliate, then retaliate" (wa in 'aqabtum fa-'aqibu), meaning: if you go on to victory, then go on with the like of what was done to you.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood over Hamza when he had been mutilated. It is also narrated: he saw him with his belly ripped open and said: "By Him by whom I swear, if Allah grants me victory over them, I will mutilate seventy of them in your place."[[Al-Tha'labi related it without a chain. I say: as for the beginning of the discussion, he mentioned it.]] Then this was revealed, so he expiated his oath and refrained from what he had intended. The phrase "the patient" is placed in the position of the pronoun as a praise from Allah for them, that they are patient in hardships; or it describes them by the attribute that comes to them when they are patient in refraining from retaliation. Or it may refer to the category of patience, which "sabartum" indicates, and "the patient" refers to its category, as if it were said: "patience is good for the patient."
